ui.comments.err.guidance: The guidance of section {n} has at most 2000 characters.
ui.comments.err.heading: Section {n} needs a heading.
ui.comments.err.long: The name has at most 200 characters and the first line, 400.
ui.comments.err.status: The template needs a first line.
ui.comments.err.title: The template needs a name.
ui.comments.event.question: An agent's question
ui.comments.f.heading: Heading
ui.comments.f.sectionsHint: They come after the status, in this order; a section with nothing to say is left out. The guidance is what the agent is told to write it.
ui.comments.f.technicalHint: A collapsed section at the end: file, function and line names go only there.
ui.comments.f.title: Name
ui.comments.f.titleHint: How the comment appears in the app's lists (Actions, the thread).
ui.comments.hint: What each stage leaves as a comment on the issue: a status first, the sections you choose and, at the end, the technical detail collapsed. A stage with no template posts nothing. The text follows the workspace language.
ui.comments.new.heading: Summary
ui.comments.noTemplate: {name} has no template: it posts no comment.
ui.comments.previewNote: A sample with made-up texts, put together the way the runner puts it together. The hidden marker at the end is not shown here.
ui.comments.saved: Templates saved. The next comment already uses the new text.
ui.comments.warn.placeholder: {name} is not something the status knows: it is left as written.
ui.flow.diagram.legend: Solid arrow: goes on. Dashed arrow: sends the work back. Hexagon: a gate, your decision. Pill: a wait.
ui.flow.empty: This flow has no stages. Add one or start from a template.
ui.flow.err.commentKey: The comment key uses lowercase letters, digits, "-" and "_".
ui.flow.err.file: "{file}" is not a plain file name: use letters, digits, ".", "-" and "_", no folder and not starting with a dot.
ui.flow.err.idShape: The id uses lowercase letters, digits, "-" and "_", and starts with a letter or a digit.
ui.flow.err.idTaken: Another stage already has the id "{id}".
ui.flow.err.minutes: Enter a number of minutes, 1 or more.
ui.flow.err.roundLimit: The limit is a number from 1 to 20.
ui.flow.err.trackerStatus: The label has at most 200 characters.
ui.flow.f.agentHint: Who works this stage. The stage where the run ends may have no agent.
ui.flow.f.commentHint: The comment template the stage posts on the tracker. Templates are edited in the Comments tab.
ui.flow.f.idHint: It names the stage's files and the marker of its comment. Changing the id takes the stages that point at it along. It applies when you leave the field.
ui.flow.f.kindHint: What the stage means to the ceremonies and the checks. A work stage that is a review or QA sends the work back when it finds problems.
ui.flow.f.name: Name
ui.flow.f.nextHint: By default, the next in the list.
ui.flow.f.producesHint: Plain names in the cycle folder (1_SPEC.md): no folder and not starting with a dot. Two stages cannot write the same file.
ui.flow.f.readsHint: The documents of the earlier stages and the issue record the stage is given.
ui.flow.f.returnsToHint: Where the work goes back to: a rejected gate, a review with problems, a QA failure.
ui.flow.f.roundLimitHint: How many times this stage may send the work back before the run stops and asks you. Empty: {count}.
ui.flow.f.trackerStatusHint: A label the issue gets on entering the stage (a write, posted under the agent's autonomy). Empty: none.
ui.flow.f.waitBetaMinutes: Minutes since the beta was published
ui.flow.f.waitBlockingLabel: Label of an issue that blocks the stable
ui.flow.f.waitBlockingLabelHint: An open issue with this label keeps the wait going. Left empty: beta-blocker.
ui.flow.import.failed: This file is not a flow the app accepts:
ui.flow.import.notFlow: The file is a cycle template, but its stages are not a flow (none has a type, an agent or what it produces).
ui.flow.listHint: Drag the stages to reorder them, or use the arrows. Where each stage goes next and where it sends work back follows the order unless you say otherwise in the panel.
ui.flow.newAgent.idNote: Id: @{id}. The agent joins the team when you save the flow.
ui.flow.newAgent.modelHint: It uses that role's model. You can change it later in the Team tab.
ui.flow.newAgent.title: New agent for this stage
ui.flow.panel.title: Stage {name}
ui.flow.replace.body: What you edited in it is lost (nothing is saved until you save). The agents the template brings that the workspace lacks are created; the ones that already exist stay as they are.
ui.flow.replace.title: Replace the flow of {target} with "{name}"?
ui.flow.runsNote: Runs in progress keep the flow they started with. The edited flow applies to new runs.
ui.flow.saved: Flow saved. New runs follow this flow.
ui.flow.squadDrop.body: Its own flow leaves the draft; it applies when you save. Runs in progress keep theirs.
ui.flow.squadDrop.title: Take the squad {name} back to the workspace's flow?
ui.flow.squadFollows: The squad {name} follows the workspace's flow. Give it a flow of its own to change only its stages.
ui.flow.squadGive: Give it a flow of its own (a copy of the current one)
ui.flow.squadOwn: The squad {name} follows a flow of its own.
ui.flow.starter.short.description: Refine, plan, implement, review and QA with no gate to stop at: review and QA still send the work back.
ui.flow.starter.short.name: Short agent cycle, no gates
ui.flow.type.gate.hint: You decide: approve, send back with a reason or skip.
ui.flow.type.wait.hint: The run waits for an event.
ui.flow.wait.beta-age: the latest beta to be out for a while with nothing blocking it
ui.flow.wait.beta-out: the latest beta to be on the host (its tag on the remote, its pre-release published)
ui.flow.wait.budget: the provider to have budget on its key again
ui.flow.wait.label: the issue gets a label
ui.flow.wait.linked-done: the runs asked of another squad to end
ui.flow.wait.release-approved: every {crLong} of the release to be merged into its branch
ui.flow.wait.stable-out: the stable to be on the host (its tag on the remote, on main)
ui.runner.capHint: From {min} to {max}. After that the stage fails and can be retried, even if the agent is still working.
ui.runner.commands: Commands an agent that writes may run
ui.runner.commandsCustomHint: Each command exactly as typed, one plain command: no pipe, ";", "&&" or redirect. An empty list: none.
ui.runner.commandsNone: None: an agent that writes runs no command.
ui.runner.commandsRepoHint: The test and typecheck scripts the repository declares (npm test, npm run typecheck).
ui.runner.commitHint: One line. {summary} becomes the agent's summary and {iid} the issue number. Follow the repository's rule.
ui.runner.concurrentHint: From 1 to 10. How many the app starts by itself while others work; the ones you start never wait.
ui.runner.enabledHint: On, the app starts a run for each issue that carries the label below. Starting a run by hand does not need it.
ui.runner.err.commandBlank: A command cannot be empty or start or end with a space.
ui.runner.err.commandPlain: "{command}" is not a plain command: no pipe, ";", "&&", redirect or substitution.
ui.runner.err.commitLong: The message has at most 200 characters.
ui.runner.err.concurrent: Use a whole number from 1 to 10.
ui.runner.err.email: The email does not look like an address.
ui.runner.err.identityPair: Enter both the name and the email, or leave both empty.
ui.runner.err.idle: Use a time from {min} to {max} minutes.
ui.runner.err.max: Use a time from {min} to {max} minutes.
ui.runner.err.sandboxHost: "{host}" is not a host name: no scheme, port, path or wildcard.
ui.runner.err.sandboxLimit: Each limit is a whole number between {min} and {max}.
ui.runner.err.sandboxPath: "{path}" must be a folder: absolute or starting with ~/, not the home folder or the root of the disk.
ui.runner.err.sandboxPathSecret: "{path}" looks like a place that holds keys, tokens or settings, or belongs to the system: a sandbox never gets it.
ui.runner.err.trigger: Enter the label: the scheduler is on.
ui.runner.err.turns: Use a whole number from {min} to {max}.
ui.runner.hint: What takes an issue through the agent cycle by itself. Nothing here gives an agent more power than the run's worktree.
ui.runner.identity: Who the app's commits are made as
ui.runner.identityHint: The app makes the commits of the agent's work in the worktree, and the merge that resolves a conflict. Both empty: the identity in the repository's own .git/config. The global git identity is never used: with neither, the app does not commit.
ui.runner.identityNone: The one in the repository's own .git/config (never the global one)
ui.runner.idle: Longest the agent may be silent (minutes)
ui.runner.idleHint: From {min} to {max}. If the agent shows no sign of life (text, a tool, model usage) for that long, the stage fails and can be retried. One that keeps working never reaches it.
ui.runner.linkDeps: Give each run the dependencies of the clone
ui.runner.linkDepsHint: A run's worktree starts with no node_modules or .venv, so the tests cannot run. On, the app links the ones your clone has (never committed); the commands it runs there use the clone's dependencies.
ui.runner.sandbox.available: This computer can make a sandbox (bubblewrap {version}).
ui.runner.sandbox.checking: Checking whether this computer can make a sandbox…
ui.runner.sandbox.hint: What the sandbox of an agent set to run commands in one may reach and use. It is built for each stage and ends with it, with everything it started.
ui.runner.sandbox.network.off.hint: Nothing leaves the sandbox. A project whose tests need packages that are not in the repository cannot install them.
ui.runner.sandbox.network.registry.hint: Only HTTPS to the hosts below, through a proxy the app runs. It is a window to those hosts and no more, but a request to a registry can carry data in its address: turn it on only when installing needs it. It needs Node inside the sandbox.
ui.runner.sandbox.pathsHint: Folders outside the worktree that every sandbox of this workspace can read, such as a toolchain installed in your home folder. Never the home folder itself, the app's data, system places (/proc, /sys, /dev, /run, /var, /tmp) or anything that looks like keys or settings. A folder that holds a repository shows its .git/config as it is (the cleaned copy is only for the run's own repository): list toolchains, not checkouts.
ui.runner.sandbox.unavailable: This computer cannot make a sandbox: {reason}.
ui.runner.soleMaintainer: I am the only maintainer of the repository
ui.runner.soleMaintainerHint: For when nobody else can review: the host does not let you approve a {crLong} you opened, so a release could never merge one. On, your yes in Actions on a release merge stands for the review of a {crLong} opened by the account the app uses on the host, on which nobody asked for changes; every release merge then waits for that yes, even with an agent that runs by itself. One that someone else opened still needs an approval on the host. Off when the repository has other reviewers.
ui.runner.soleMaintainerOff: Off: a release merge needs an approval on the host
ui.runner.soleMaintainerOn: On: your yes on a release merge stands for the review of your own {crLongs}
ui.runner.trigger: Label that asks for a run
ui.runner.turnsRead: Steps for an agent that only reads
ui.runner.turnsReadHint: From {min} to {max}. How many steps (model turns) it has in one pass, to read and write the stage's documents. When they run out, the stage fails. It is also the limit of an agent called with @ in a thread, of a question in the chain and of a request between agents: those answer with what they have read when it runs out.
ui.runner.turnsWrite: Steps for an agent that changes files
ui.runner.turnsWriteHint: From {min} to {max}. The same, for one that changes code and runs the allowed commands.
ui.runner.warn.idleLonger: The silence limit is longer than the stage limit: the stage limit ends the stage first.
ui.runner.warn.noCommands: With no commands, an agent that writes cannot run the tests.
ui.runner.warn.notFlow: The current cycle is not an agent flow (no stage has a type): the scheduler will not start runs.
ui.runner.warn.registryOn: The registry switch is on: the sandbox can reach the listed hosts, and only them.
ui.runner.webNote: From the browser you change what runs and when. The folder for the runs, the commands and who the commits are made as are changed on the computer.
ui.runner.worktreesHint: Where the worktrees are made ("~/" works). Empty: the worktrees folder of the workspace's data.
ui.sandbox.reason.platform: only Linux with bubblewrap is supported
ui.sandbox.reason.refused: the system does not let bubblewrap make a sandbox (user namespaces may be off)
ui.squads.autonomyHint: Off, every member waits for you, even with its own switch on. On, each agent's own switch applies.
ui.squads.delete.effect: The members become shared and its own flow goes. Nothing is deleted from the runs.
ui.squads.delete.noRuns: No active run is in this squad.
ui.squads.delete.title: Delete the squad {name}?
ui.squads.err.idShape: The id uses lowercase letters, digits, "-" and "_", and starts with a letter or a digit.
ui.squads.err.idTaken: There is already a squad with the id "{id}".
ui.squads.err.label: The label is one: no comma and no line break.
ui.squads.err.liaisonMember: The liaison must be one of the members.
ui.squads.err.name: Give the squad a name.
ui.squads.err.path: Each folder needs a repository and a path.
ui.squads.f.label: Label on the issue
ui.squads.f.labelHint: The issue gets this label on the tracker when a run starts in the squad. Empty: none.
ui.squads.f.liaisonHint: Who gets the questions and requests of the other squads and speaks for the squad. Required when there are members.
ui.squads.f.membersHint: An agent belongs to one squad: ticking one that belongs to another brings it here.
ui.squads.f.missionHint: What the squad is for, in a sentence. The agents read it.
ui.squads.f.name: Name
ui.squads.f.pathsHint: For a monorepo split by folders: an issue that mentions a file inside the folder is the squad's.
ui.squads.f.scopeHint: Which work is the squad's. The repository decides first, then the labels, then the folders the issue text mentions.
ui.squads.f.unclaimedHint: Use it on one squad: the issues no scope takes go to it.
ui.squads.flow.ownHint: This squad follows a flow of its own. A run that already started keeps the flow it started with.
ui.squads.flow.workspaceHint: This squad follows the workspace's flow. You can give it a flow of its own in the flow editor.
ui.squads.hint: A squad has a scope, members, a flow and a liaison, the agent that speaks for it to the other squads. With no squads, the workspace is one team.
ui.squads.label: Label
ui.squads.none: No squads: the workspace works as one team.
ui.team.allowed.hint: Commands you allowed this agent always when it asked. A "prefix:*" rule allows the command and anything after it; a command that writes to the code host is asked every time.
ui.team.allowed.title: Always allowed in the ceremonies
ui.team.autonomyHint: Off, the stage waits for you to start it, what it posts waits for your yes in Actions and its result waits for you to accept it. Pushing the branch and opening the {crLong} always wait for you.
ui.team.delete.lose: These stages are left with no agent (the flow warns until you pick another):
ui.team.delete.noneLost: No stage depends on it alone.
ui.team.delete.title: Delete {name}?
ui.team.err.allowlist: Listed commands run in the real worktree, so they need the permission to change files. An agent that only reads runs commands in a sandbox.
ui.team.err.idReserved: "{id}" is the id of a built-in agent.
ui.team.err.idShape: The id uses lowercase letters, digits, "-" and "_", and starts with a letter or a digit.
ui.team.err.idTaken: There is already an agent with the id "{id}".
ui.team.err.name: Give the agent a name.
ui.team.f.idHint: It is also the mention name (@id). It does not change later.
ui.team.f.instructionsHint: They go into the agent's prompt, after the team's instructions.
ui.team.f.jobHint: What the agent does, in a sentence or two.
ui.team.f.name: Name
ui.team.f.squadHint: An agent belongs to one squad. Shared, it works for every squad.
ui.team.f.turnsToHint: Who gets the question first, before it reaches you. The chain ends with you.
ui.team.heldBySquad: The squad's switch is off: this agent waits for you while it stays that way.
ui.team.hint: Each agent has a job, a model and a permission. The switch lets the agent run by itself: its stage starts when the run reaches it and what it posts on the issue goes out without waiting for your yes.
ui.team.intro: Who works each stage, how the work moves from one to the next and what each stage leaves on the issue. It applies to new runs; a run in progress keeps the flow it started with.
ui.team.model.name: Model
ui.team.model.role.hint: Uses the provider and model you chose for that role in Models.
ui.team.model.role.label: Role
ui.team.permission.read.hint: Reads the run's files and writes only the stage's documents.
ui.team.permission.worktree.hint: Also changes files and runs the allowed commands, inside the run's worktree and nowhere else.
ui.team.rec.hint: The agents below do not have what their role is recommended to have: the Product Owner and the Tech Lead read the code host, and QA, the developer and the Tech Lead run commands in a sandbox. Nothing changes until you apply it.
ui.team.rec.noSandbox: This computer has no sandbox, so the commands stay as the agents could run them before sandboxes existed.
ui.team.rec.title: Recommended permissions
ui.team.shell.allowlist.hint: Runs only the commands listed in the runner settings, exactly as written, in the worktree. They are not sandboxed.
ui.team.shell.host.hint: Runs any command on this computer, as you, outside any sandbox: it reaches the network, your tools, containers and emulators. Each command waits for you to allow it (once, or for the rest of the stage) on this computer, or on a paired phone only when external effects are allowed there. An agent that only reads runs them in a throwaway copy of the code. Set only here, never by a template.
ui.team.shell.noSandboxWeb: A sandbox is not offered on the computer running the app.
ui.team.shell.readerCopy: An agent that only reads works in a throwaway copy of the code: nothing it does reaches the branch.
ui.team.shell.sandbox.hint: Runs any command inside a sandbox: the worktree is writable, the rest of the system is read-only, nothing of your home folder, no credentials, no network unless the runner settings allow the package registry. Never pushes or writes to the code host.
ui.team.systemNote: A built-in agent: it can be edited but not deleted. The ceremonies use its model and instructions.
ui.team.title: Team and cycle
ui.team.tools.files.hint: Reading the code and searching it. Never Edit or Write.
ui.team.tools.hint: What this agent may use, overriding the workspace's tools field by field: turn one on here and it uses it even when the workspace turned it off. It does not give the agent a way to change files in a conversation.
ui.team.tools.skills.hint: The Claude Code skills of the configured folders.
ui.team.tools.subagents.hint: Delegating a broad search to a subagent, in the ceremonies.
ui.team.tools.trackerMcp.hint: The issue tracker's own tools, when a server is configured.
ui.team.tools.trackerMcpServer.hint: The MCP server that offers the issue tools; empty: none.
ui.team.tools.vcsCli.hint: Read-only use of the code host's own command line.
ui.team.tracker.none.hint: Reads nothing from the code host in a run: it works from the issue record, the documents and the code.
ui.team.tracker.read.hint: Reads issues and comments and, in the {crLongs} that mention them, the diff, the review threads and the checks. Never writes: writing stays in Actions. Uses the read path the workspace has on; with none, there is nothing to read with.
